# Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps — concept pack (small)

> Source-anchored research for Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps. Run status: COMPLETED.

## How it works

- [statement] MongoDB documents this inclusive M30–M60 General-class boundary: forbid(principal, action == ResourcePolicy::Action::"cluster.modify", resource) when { (context.cluster has minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue && context.cluster.minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue < 30) || (context.cluster has maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue && context.cluster.maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue > 60) }; (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources to detect existing violations and remediate them; applying a policy does not automatically rewrite pre-existing configurations. The independent Foojay walkthrough demonstrates unchanged but flagged resources. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Guard optional attributes before comparing them. Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation; MongoDB’s tier example uses has checks. Whether Atlas adds stricter runtime error handling is not established here. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] The minGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue and maxGeneralClassInstanceSizeValue attributes represent the current tier or the minimum and maximum autoscaling sizes; author against these bounds rather than checking only a desired current tier. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
- [statement] Cedar skips policies that error during evaluation. Issue #2428 illustrates incorrect string membership using in, corrected with set.contains(value), and maintainers identify it as invalid unvalidated policy rather than an engine bug. This is a general authoring caution, not evidence of an Atlas exploit. (high confidence) — https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://github.com/cedar-policy/cedar/issues/2428
- [statement] A practitioner walkthrough reports successful Terraform deployment and blocked noncompliant requests, but does not demonstrate enforcement of a tier or autoscaling cap. Treat its cap discussion as guidance rather than an independent cap test. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-08-13) — https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Atlas Resource Policies add organization-wide configuration guardrails to RBAC; project exceptions allow narrower application. Cluster tier caps are a documented cost-control use. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/decoupling-authorization-at-scale-mongodb-atlas-and-cedar-based-resource-policies/
- [statement] MongoDB explicitly excludes Low CPU and NVMe SSD classes from its sample General class tier restriction; do not describe that sample as a universal instance-size cap. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
- [statement] Atlas accepts forbid policies, excludes permit statements, and allows role-authorized operations by default. Generic Cedar instead defaults to denial without a matching permit; do not transfer its default directly to Atlas. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://docs.cedarpolicy.com/auth/authorization.html
- [statement] Existing autoscaling bounds can exceed a newly introduced policy and continue scaling beyond it, although manual scaling beyond the policy is blocked. Inspect /orgs/{ORG-ID}/nonCompliantResources and reconcile existing bounds. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
- [statement] Manage resource policies as code with the MongoDB Atlas Terraform provider; an independently authored Foojay walkthrough embeds Cedar bodies in mongodbatlas_resource_policy, while the organization module supports applying policies to existing organizations. (high confidence) — https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://github.com/terraform-mongodbatlas-modules/terraform-mongodbatlas-organization, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/decoupling-authorization-at-scale-mongodb-atlas-and-cedar-based-resource-policies/
- [statement] Upper and lower cluster tier constraints were publicly announced on March 3, 2025 for provisioning, scaling and updates; this dated preview announcement is historical evidence, not a statement of current preview status. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-03-03) — https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/now-in-public-preview-two-more-atlas-resource-policies-to-manage-cluster-sizes-and-maintenance-windows/314568 · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
- [statement] The min/max General-class context values cover the current tier and autoscaling bounds. The example does not constrain Low CPU or NVMe SSD clusters. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/
- [statement] Terraform can carry Cedar in mongodbatlas_resource_policy policies[].body, with org_id and name. Versioning policies alongside infrastructure enables reviewable, repeatable governance changes. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-18) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/atlas-resource-policies/ · keywords: Cedar policy authoring for cluster size and autoscaling caps · also: https://foojay.io/today/enforcing-governance-in-mongodb-atlas-with-resource-policies/, https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/opensource/decoupling-authorization-at-scale-mongodb-atlas-and-cedar-based-resource-policies/
